literatureReview.rejectedRoss614GaiaEstimates: Cifuentes 2025 Table A.1 explicitly flags Ross 614 B: Gaia G magnitude does not match WDS difference. Its nearly equal A/B photometric masses and radii are not adopted. The 10pc census also marks the purported Gaia component identification doubtful. Retain resolved dynamical masses instead.
literatureReview.flVirRemainingGaps: Cifuentes 2025 radii are photometric MG-calibration estimates in an orbit/blend-affected pair (RUWE 6.12/13.95, IPDfmp 58/40). Not adopted as high-quality radii. Houdebine 2019 temperature is unresolved and is not duplicated to both components. No resolved bolometric luminosity, reliable abundance or age adopted.
literatureReview.ross614MassDisagreement: Adopt internally consistent resolved HST/RV masses 0.223/0.109 solar from Benedict 2016, already reviewed for the effective components. Feng 2022 gives a lower secondary mass with a different joint fit; retain that disagreement here rather than mixing one fit with a different primary mass. Radius/luminosity/age remain unavailable pending defensible component measurements.
literatureReview.gj1245AtmosphereCaveats: Dieterich 2021 Table 2 supplies resolved A/C fits with 109 K temperature error and 5 percent radius systematic scatter. Authors caution that fits deteriorate at these temperatures, especially C, and that metallicities are systematically subsolar; fitted abundances and age are not adopted. Component luminosities are model-derived, not direct flux measurements.

gj1245RadialVelocityAlternative.decision: More recent B measurement is consistent with the adopted 5.43 +/-0.10 km/s (Morin 2010). Retain the existing conservative value as the shared bulk proxy; do not turn the small 2018 formal error into a systemic-motion accuracy.
